briefing.headline: OpenAI o4-preview and xAI Colossus push AGI timelines forward amid rising compute arms race

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs released multiple high-capability models this month while regulatory pressure builds in the US and EU. Funding remains robust with major rounds closing in infrastructure and safety tooling. Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems as multi-agent deployments accelerate.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed o4-preview with advanced reasoning while Anthropic's Claude 4 Opus and Google's Gemini 2.5 Ultra entered testing. Meta open-sourced Llama 4 405B variant and DeepSeek released R2. xAI activated Colossus-2 cluster targeting 1M H100 equivalents by Q4.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: New jailbreak techniques targeting agentic workflows surfaced on arXiv. Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for multi-agent, automotive, and BCI applications.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA shipped Blackwell B200 in volume to hyperscalers. Microsoft and Oracle announced 50GW data center expansions focused on AI training. TSMC reported record AI chip orders for 2026.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first 10^26 FLOP training run occur before or after 2028 regulatory harmonization?
